thread:
olivia: heads up — seeing a burst of GPU evictions in ap-southeast1 since ~06:10 UTC. pods keep bouncing with preempt/evict reasons, stacktrace points at scheduler placement conflicts. anyone digging? :thinking:
diego: yep noticed it on dashboards, eviction rate ~4.8% for gpu workloads. trace looks like preferred nodeAffinity wins flipped after a cross-region provision event. kube-scheduler logs:
```
E0601 06:11:22.123 scheduler.go:789] pod default/model-train-7 couldn't find node: PreferredDuringScheduling affinity constraints could not be met, weight sum 100 -> rejected
E0601 06:11:22.125 scheduler.go:792] Evicting pod model-train-7 from node gpu-shelf-3
```
maya: FYI the provisioner fired a resync and provisioned 8 new GPU nodes in ap-southeast2 then applied labels from the hardware catalog. I suspect label mismatch (gpu-flavor vs gpu-type) + taint reserved=true toggles the fast path for placement and triggers reshuffle. cost alert popped when extra backfills hit burst capacity. @raj can you check the provisioner rollout?
raj: looking now — provisioner autoscaler scaled up due to regional threshold. It labels nodes as `gpu-flavor=rtx6000` (from hw catalog) but older nodes are labeled `gpu-type=v100`. Our scheduler policies treat those as non-interchangeable for affinity weights, so pods pinned to v100s got considered unschedulable on the new nodes and we triggered evictions to re-place them. Also noticed the provisioner briefly applied taint `reserved=true:NoSchedule` during init, then removed it; race between taint removal and label normalization likely caused bounce.
olivia: ah that explains it. So new nodes were fine but scheduler logic + temporary taint caused a window where pods were preempted instead of being accepted. Any quick mitigation?
diego: quick hack — we can push a node-label-mapping admission job to normalize `gpu-flavor` -> `gpu-type` for the provisioned nodes, and patch the provisioner to stop mutating taint during label writes. Doing that should stop the churn.
jun: long-term we should add a label equivalence map in the scheduler policy (or model-group annotation) so preferredDuringScheduling counts equivalent families as match. Right now weights are strict exact-match which makes these cross-generation upgrades noisy. Also add a short TTL on eviction decisions when a node has transient taints removed in the last Xs.
raj: will open a quick PR to patch the provisioner to emit both labels (gpu-type and gpu-flavor) and to delay removing `reserved=true` until kubelet ready heartbeat confirmed. Patch ETA ~30m.
sre-bot: ALERT: evictions > 3% in channel ap-southeast1 for 18m, triggered incident runbook 'gpu-evict-churn' — runbook assigned to oncall.
maya: for rollback if PR doesn't land fast, we can temporarily add `tolerations:` for `reserved=true` to the deployment spec of training jobs (risk of letting init nodes serve non-intended workloads) — tradeoff is lower churn vs possible noisy collocation.
olivia: agreed — prefer normalized labels + scheduler map. raj plz post PR link and we can coordinate canary. also add a short prometheus alert for label-mismatch churn so we catch this earlier. :thumbsup:
raj: PR: https://git.internal/r/provisioner/merge_requests/482 — adds dual-label emit + taint hold. canarying to ap-southeast2 only. will update here when rolled.
diego: after deploy, will run a small job to probe placement for v100-affine pods and report eviction delta. if churn drops under 1% we close the followup.
olivia: thanks team — logged followups: (1) scheduler equivalence mapping RFC, (2) provisioner dual-label rollout, (3) short TTL on eviction decisions. keeping channel updated.
